themes.theme: Strait of Hormuz energy flow normalization
themes.consensus_view: After the US-Iran deal, banks across seven desks agree oil is flowing back through the Strait of Hormuz and the war-risk premium in oil prices is unwinding, but nobody has staked out a clear next directional call.

facts_agreed.claim: Banks consistently reference the Strait of Hormuz as a live energy-flow topic, framing it around disruption risk now giving way to normalization after the Iran deal.
evidence_quotes: Strait of Hormuz energy flow normalization

facts_agreed.claim: Oil prices fell sharply, roughly 10-25 percent, as the Middle East war-risk premium unwound following the US-Iran deal.

themes.theme: Middle East conflict supply bottleneck risks
themes.consensus_view: Five banks reference the Middle East conflict and its effect on oil supply as a live macro factor, but with a post-deal peace agreement now reopening Gulf flows nobody is staking a clear directional view on prices.

themes.consensus_view: Banks across several desks treat the US-Iran peace deal as a real market event that is reopening Gulf oil flows and pulling oil prices down, but no desk has staked a clear directional bet on what happens next.

facts_agreed.claim: The US-Iran deal is reopening Gulf oil flows and easing the war-risk premium that had been lifting oil prices.

themes.consensus_view: The Fed is being read as firmly recommitted to its 2% inflation goal, with new leadership signaling that holding prices steady is now a non-negotiable priority.

evidence_quotes: This Committee will deliver price stability.

themes.consensus_view: UBS reads the May inflation data as evidence the Fed's policy shift may be less aggressive than markets first feared, while the rest of the corpus only references rate-policy in passing without staking a directional view.
